newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX weaker despite rise in MOL.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX weaker despite rise in MOL.

text.p: The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange lost ground on Friday in an apparent sign that investors unloaded other stocks to replace by shares in oil company MOL, traders said.
"People focus on MOL: sell others in order to buy MOL instead," said Laszlo Baranyai of Gog Securities.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 5,944.46 points, down 26.44.
Traders said that MOL's market moving role, after its six-times oversubscribed global offering and before a domestic public offer which starts on Monday, was undoubted.
"Once again MOL was the main attraction, in terms of both price movements and turnover," another trader said.
"I doubt that international trends left any substantial impact on the market today," he said. "MOL and (drugs maker) Richter have been the key driving forces on the market in the past few days."
More than one million MOL shares changed hands on Friday as the market was waiting for the start of its domestic offer.
MOL closed at 3,475 forints, up 15, but below the day's peak of 3,635 forints.
MOL's closing price below the day's highest level was explained by arbitrage between its price in Budapest and on the SEAQ in London.
"One brokerage took advantage from arbitrage opportunities between London and Budapest," the trader said. "Therefore the (lower) closing price isn't a miracle."
Richter ran out of steam after an early rally to a new record high of 15,180 forints and retreated to end at 14,900, down 50.

"Richter's market turned to be overheated in light of its share issue later this month," the trader said. "Richter's high price is also strange because of the gap between Richter and Egis is almost 50 percent."
"Egis is not that bad compared to Egis as their prices reflect." Egis closed at 10,650 forints, down 320.
Elsewhere on the market, some less liquid stocks, such as Fotex group member furniture trader Domus gained more than 23 percent to 470 forints, while tourism company Ibusz gaining 15 percent to 690.
Both trade below their 1,000 forints face value.

All beverage companies gave up some, with mineral water bottler Kekkuti and liquer maker Zwack each falling 50 forints to 1,100 forints and 4,000 forints, respectively, while brewery Sopron easing 85 to 5,805.
